edits.from: The Masoretic Text and the Judean Desert Hebrew manuscript 4QGenb (4Q2) move directly from 'And Cain said to Abel his brother' to the scene in the field, without recording Cain's words. The Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and Vulgate preserve a clause equivalent to, 'Let us go out to the field.'
edits.to: The Masoretic Text does not record Cain's words. The surviving wording in 4QGenb (4Q2), as published, supports this shorter transition. The Samaritan Pentateuch and Greek Septuagint include, “Let us go to the field.” The Latin Vulgate has, “Let us go outside”; the Syriac Peshitta similarly includes an invitation to the plain. Whether the invitation was lost from the shorter form or added to complete it is disputed.
edits.rationale: Insert exactly independently approved note: published partial 4Q2 junction, distinct versional wording, priority unresolved.

edits.from: This is primarily a textual decision rather than a doctrinal one. The shorter MT is abrupt, while multiple ancient witnesses preserve the speech, but coherence by itself does not prove that the longer form is earlier. Direct Hebrew witness 4QGenb (4Q2) demonstrates that the shorter form was already in circulation in the Judean Desert period. The current text therefore retains the shorter wording while image verification and formal adjudication remain outstanding.
edits.to: This is primarily a textual decision rather than a doctrinal one. The published transcription of 4QGenb (4Q2) supports the shorter junction in surviving wording, while much of the speech introduction is supplied. The consulted Samaritan Hebrew and Greek texts include an invitation; the Latin and Syriac versions phrase it differently. An invitation could have been lost before the shorter Hebrew witnesses or added to complete an abrupt utterance. The comparison and independent note-proposal review do not settle historical priority, and no fresh manuscript-image or exhaustive apparatus review is claimed.
